claim_being_audited: Whether the current release can be certified on the basis that aggregate readiness passed, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the known developer-support migration weakness can be handled through disclosure or approved mitigation.
decision_criteria: If current release documentation explicitly discloses the material segment weakness, certification could be compliant under the stated policy.
If an approved current mitigation or risk acceptance covers the weakness, certification could be compliant even without full resolution.
If neither current disclosure nor approved mitigation exists, certification should not proceed under the policy.
Aggregate readiness and clean rehearsal are supportive but do not override the policy requirement for current handling of material segment weaknesses.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model-card or certification document showing the developer-support migration weakness is explicitly disclosed.
Provide a reviewed and approved mitigation or risk-acceptance record covering that specific segment weakness for the current release.
Provide the current evaluation artifact tying the subgroup regression to the exact release under certification.
Provide the approval or sign-off showing the current release documentation was reviewed with the limitation included.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and requires material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation.
The actor summary itself says the packet lacks attached reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language for the subgroup weakness.
The developer-support migration slice is described as below the warning threshold, which makes the unresolved handling of that weakness material to certification.
Prior approval from four months ago is explicitly contextual only under the policy and cannot substitute for current-release support.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify the model is not evidentially supported on the current packet because required disclosure or approved mitigation is not shown.
The statement that the weakness can be explicitly disclosed in the model card is forward-looking; no attached disclosure text or current documentation evidence is provided.
Any implication that the subgroup weakness is already adequately handled for this release is unsupported by the available evidence summary.
